title: Sliding windows and prefix sums
summary: Reuse yesterday's work: slide a window instead of re-adding it, and answer range sums in O(1).

steps.title: Slide, don't recompute
body: What is the largest sum of `k` consecutive items? Adding up every window from scratch costs `O(n × k)`.

But neighbouring windows overlap in all but two items. Slide the window one step: **add** the item that enters on the right, **subtract** the one that leaves on the left. Each step is `O(1)`, the whole scan `O(n)`.
Watch `window` change by just two items at a time.

code: for (var i = 0; i < k; i++) window += a[i];
for (var right = k; right < a.Length; right++)

steps.prompt: Windows of size 2. What does it print?
code: for (var i = 0; i < k; i++) window += a[i];
for (var right = k; right < a.Length; right++)
steps.explain: The window sums are 6, 14, 15, 4, 10. The best is `12 + 3`.

steps.title: Windows that stretch and shrink
body: Sometimes the window size is the answer. **Longest run of characters with no repeats**: grow the window on the right; whenever the new character is already inside, shrink from the left until it is not.
Each character enters once and leaves at most once, so it is `O(n)` even with the inner `while`.

steps.prompt: The same window on `"pwwkew"`. What does it print?
steps.explain: The second `w` forces the window to shrink past the first one. Then `wke` (or `kew`) has length 3. `pwke` does not count: it is not consecutive.

steps.title: Prefix sums
body: Asked for `sum(a[l..r])` thousands of times? Precompute once: `prefix[i]` is the sum of the first `i` items, with `prefix[0] = 0`.
Then any range sum is one subtraction:
`O(n)` to build, `O(1)` per query. The extra slot at the front removes every special case for `l = 0`.

steps.prompt: Complete the range sum, `l` and `r` inclusive.
code: int RangeSum(int[] prefix, int l, int r) => prefix[__1__] - prefix[__2__];

steps.prompt: Prefix sums answer range **sums** in O(1). Which of these can they also answer in O(1) per query, with the same idea?
options: How many even numbers lie in `a[l..r]` (prefix counts)
Whether `a[l..r]` is sorted, with no other precomputation
steps.explain: Anything you can add up and subtract works: counts, sums, XORs. A maximum cannot be "subtracted away", so it needs other structures.

steps.title: Two windows
prompt: - `int MaxWindowSum(int[] a, int k)`: the largest sum of `k` consecutive items (`1 <= k <= a.Length`).
- `int LongestUnique(string s)`: the length of the longest run of consecutive characters with no repeats.
The tests use 500,000 items and a 500,000-character string.
solution: for (var i = 0; i < k; i++) window += a[i];
for (var right = k; right < a.Length; right++)
template: Dojo.Eq("MaxWindowSum k = 1 is the max", 12, MaxWindowSum(new[] { 4, 2, 12, 3 }, 1));
Dojo.Eq("MaxWindowSum k = n is the total", 21, MaxWindowSum(new[] { 4, 2, 12, 3 }, 4));
hints: `MaxWindowSum`: sum the first `k`, then for each new right item add it and subtract `a[right - k]`.
`LongestUnique`: a `HashSet<char>` of what is inside the window; shrink from the left while the new character is already inside.

steps.title: Range sums on demand
prompt: - constructor `RangeSum(int[] a)`: builds the prefix array once (use `long`, sums can be large).
- `long Sum(int l, int r)`: the sum of `a[l..r]`, inclusive, in `O(1)`.
The tests ask 200,000 questions about a 200,000-item array.
starter: public long Sum(int l, int r) => 0;
solution: for (var i = 0; i < a.Length; i++) prefix[i + 1] = prefix[i] + a[i];
public long Sum(int l, int r) => prefix[r + 1] - prefix[l];
template: for (var dojoQ = 0; dojoQ < 200_000; dojoQ++) dojoTotal += dojoBig.Sum(dojoQ / 2, 199_999 - dojoQ / 2);
Dojo.Check("200,000 queries finish in time", dojoTotal > 0, "sums should be positive");
